end.summary:
Practised identifying quadrants from the signs of an ordered pair.
Harsh correctly identified (2, -3) as being in Quadrant IV.
Reviewed the origin (0, 0) and why it is a reference point on the axes.
Harsh treated (3, 2) and (2, 3) as the same point across three responses; this was not corrected by the last seen response.
Plotted or identified the point (4, 3).
end.parentNote: Asha practised reading coordinates, using the signs of x and y to identify a quadrant, and locating the origin. Harsh explained that a negative y moves a point down and correctly used this for (2, -3). They mixed up the order of coordinates and continued to say that (3, 2) and (2, 3) are the same point; this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, have Harsh mark (3, 2) and (2, 3) on the same grid and describe the horizontal and vertical moves separately.
